subject: science

entries: Food chains: arrows follow energy flow: a chain runs producer to primary consumer to secondary consumer, and arrows point from food to feeder, the way energy moves.
slots.label: Food chains
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Food webs: one dot splits into two: one producer can feed several consumers and one consumer can have several foods, so energy splits across interlinked pathways.
slots.label: Food webs
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Pyramid of energy: only 10% moves up: most energy is lost as heat and waste, so each level keeps only a tenth and food chains stay short.
slots.label: Pyramid of energy
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The carbon cycle: one dot, round and round: photosynthesis draws CO2 into plants, respiration and combustion return it to the air, and decomposers release carbon from dead matter.
slots.label: The carbon cycle
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Conservation: when habitat shrinks, species vanish: fragmentation isolates small populations, and protected corridors reconnect fragments so species can move again.
slots.label: Conservation
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: energy is not recycled: energy flows one way and leaves as heat, while matter such as carbon is what actually cycles.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A feeding level in a food chain or web: producers are the first level, herbivores the second, and carnivores the levels above.
slots.label: Trophic level
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A sequence of trophic levels showing who eats whom, with arrows pointing in the direction of energy flow, from food to feeder.
slots.label: Food chain
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: All the interlinked food chains in a community, showing every feeding pathway energy can take.
slots.label: Food web
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A diagram of the energy at each trophic level, narrowing upwards because only about 10% of energy moves up each level.
slots.label: Pyramid of energy
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An organism, usually a green plant, that captures sunlight by photosynthesis and feeds the whole food chain or web.
slots.label: Producer
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An organism that obtains energy by eating other organisms: primary consumers eat producers, secondary consumers eat herbivores.
slots.label: Consumer
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An organism that breaks down dead matter and waste, releasing carbon and other matter back into cycles.
slots.label: Decomposer
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The cycling of carbon between air, living organisms and decomposers: photosynthesis draws CO2 in, respiration and combustion return it.
slots.label: Carbon cycle
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
